title: The Ophan in the Sky
eyebrow: Build plan for approval, round 5 · issue #418, the Ophan of Hours · your answers through 2026-10-27 · nothing built yet
replyPrefix: Build plan approved: ophan in the sky, picks

short.lead: The Ophan hangs far off in the sky, a kilometre or more from the castle, so large it dwarfs it. Its eye follows its target as they move: whoever carries the most worth, then the next down the list. Its rings spin faster or slower with what it is doing, and its eye glows and grows as it charges to full blast, with a similar tell for the lock-on. It appears 60 seconds before the portal closes with a loud hum and screen shake. Its slow beam locks on over 3 seconds and drains health fast; cover stops it. Its charged beam kills in one hit and can break cover. A beam on the carrier of the wanted piece lifts the piece into the sky, spares them, and sends the Ophan away. Nine things are still open under Choices, each with my suggestion marked.
short.hint: Tap a step to see what it creates and what it needs from you.
items: Settled: arrival 1A 2B 3* 4* 5B 6A 7*, beam 1* 2A 3A, your scale photos, far off in the sky, and the eye, rings and tells

Wanted means any piece flagged IsArtifact until the demand (#419) exists. It targets whoever carries the most and keeps hunting after a kill. It stays in the sky and never chases or catches. The slow beam locks on over 3 seconds; getting under cover escapes it, and walls block it. The charged beam kills in one hit and can take cover down. A beam on the carrier lifts the wanted piece into the sky; they live and it leaves. Its warning is a loud hum and screen shake. Its size comes from your two photos. Recorded in docs/6-decisions/Decisions.md, 2026-10-27. Its eye follows its target as they move, choosing whoever carries the most worth, then down the list. Its rings spin faster or slower by state. Its eye glows and grows while charging, up to full blast, with a similar tell for the lock-on.
This plan and the five picks below
A decisions-log entry, the systems doc, and the build starts on the branch AjsAgent/ophan-arrival-418.
Your picks, sent with "Build plan approved: ophan in the sky".
The Ophan appears in the sky

A prefab of the Ophan with its Animator on TheOphanOfHours_Rig. HuntWindowSeconds (60 s) before the portal closes, it plays its 4-second arrival clip high over the castle, and every machine hears the hum and feels the shake. A test switch forces a hunted raid until the quota (#419) exists. Its eye turns to follow its target every frame, and its three rings spin at a speed set by what it is doing.
Nothing until the build is shown.

The slow beam: a 3-second lock, then health drains while nothing blocks the line from the Ophan to you. The charged beam: one hit, and it breaks the cover it passes through, as set under Choices. A hit on a carrier lifts the wanted piece away instead. Deaths go through the same path as the Wick's catch, so every machine sees them. The beam numbers sit on the Ophan's own component, the way the Wick's numbers sit on the guard; the #433 asset keeps exactly its approved fields.
Nothing until the build is shown.

Tests for the arrival, a hit with an artifact, a hit without one, and leaving once paid. A co-op check where the Ophan strikes the client, with screenshots from both machines that I look at. Then both full suites, the raid-length check, the Wick check and the lair check.
Once it passes, a pull request into staging carries "Manual co-op test still owed".
Whether it reads as a threat you cannot fight.

The player's camera cuts it off today
Its far clip plane is 1000 m; the Ophan sits 700 m to 1.2 km away.

This is the same courtyard view as option B, drawn with the player's own camera setting: everything beyond 1000 m is not drawn, so only a sliver of the Ophan shows. The build raises the player camera's far clip plane to 3000 m. That is one setting, and the castle is small enough that it costs nothing measurable. Fog is off in raids today; the castle's light haze only softens the Ophan's lower edge.

changes: new
The rig can do all of it
The eye and the three rings are their own bones, and the pupil already glows.

Checked in the model file: the GreatWheel, InnerWheel and TiltWheel bones each carry their own ring (3,530, 1,600 and 1,634 vertices), and the Eye bone carries the eye (1,049 vertices). Code can turn and scale those four bones every frame after the animation plays, so the eye can follow a player and the rings can speed up and slow down without new clips. Its one material has an emission map, so the glow can be raised from code. The pupil is the part that glows, at nine times brightness (docs/4-systems/raid-scene-assembly.md).
new
What the castle can break today
Walls and floors are one piece, and rooms have no roofs.

Each room's floor and four walls are a single mesh with a single collider, so no wall can be removed without the floor going too. No room has a roof: the sky is open above every room, and only the crypt and the keep's lower storey have anything overhead. Door plugs are the only separate pieces. The castle is never sent over the network: every machine builds it from one shared seed, so any broken wall needs its own sync.
new
What a beam looks like from a kilometre away
A thin line would vanish; it has to be drawn huge.

At a kilometre, a beam two metres wide is a tenth of a degree across, too thin to see. So the beam is drawn tens of metres wide where it leaves the eye, narrowing to a pool of light on the target, and it glows. Because the source is so far away, the warning has to show at the eye itself: the eye brightens through the 3-second lock and the charge, which every player can see wherever they stand.
choices: size
How big, and how far off? (It always faces the castle, eye first, and never comes near it.)
A
52 times its model, 600 m out: 63% of the view's height
Large, but it sits in the sky rather than filling it.
B
117 times its model, 1 km out: 84% of the view's height
Fills most of the view; you can take it in at a glance.
C
150 times its model, 900 m out: more than the whole view
You cannot take it all in at once; you look up and around to see it, which is what taking up the sky means.
Farther off also means it looks the same from everywhere in the castle: it never seems to come closer.
wings
You asked for it wider. Its wings rise in a V, so on screen it is taller than it is wide. Spread them?
A
Yes: a new held pose with the wings spread flat, so it is about half again as wide as it is tall
About a day in the art pipeline: one new pose on the existing rig, checked on a review sheet like the other clips.
B
No: keep the V; the size alone is enough
The model is 11 m across and 9.6 m tall; only a pose change makes it read wider.
worth
What does "most worth" mean when it picks its target?
A
The sell value of the piece a player is carrying, the same worth the portal's tally counts
The same number the haul is judged by, so carrying the best loot is what makes you the target.
B
Artifacts first, then sell value
Whoever holds an artifact is always first.
C
Weight carried
Your rule: the most worth first, then down the list.
rings
Which state spins the rings fastest?
A
Charging the charged beam is fastest, winding up to full blast; the lock-on is half that; hanging and watching is a slow turn; leaving, they spin down to a stop
The faster the rings, the closer the blow, so you can read its state from anywhere.
B
The lock-on is fastest, and the charge slows them to a grinding stop before the blast
Speed tells you what is coming.
tells
How does the lock-on's tell differ from the charge's?
A
Lock-on: the eye narrows and pulses, the pulse quickening over the 3 seconds. Charge: the eye swells to half again its size and brightens steadily to full blast
A quickening pulse means move now; a swelling glow means get out of the way of what comes next. They read differently at a glance.
B
Both glow and grow, in different colours: gold for the lock-on, white for the charge
C
The lock-on shows only by the eye turning on you; only the charge glows
Both tells sit at the eye, which every player can see from anywhere.
hum
The hum: you wrote "a loud menstrual hum". Which did you mean?
A
A monstrous hum: a low, loud drone for the 4-second arrival, made in code until real audio exists, with the existing camera shake
There is no Ophan sound in the project yet; a generated drone is a stand-in you can replace. The game already has a camera-shake system.
B
Another word: tell me
A stand-in hum now, real audio later.
numbers
The beams' numbers
A
Slow beam: 25 health a second (4 seconds from full). Charged beam: it charges for 3 seconds once its target has been behind cover for 3 seconds, then waits 10 seconds before it can charge again
Fast enough to frighten, slow enough to reach cover; hiding works for a moment, then it blasts the cover.
B
Slow beam 50 a second (2 seconds); charged beam on a fixed timer every 15 seconds
C
Slow beam 15 a second (about 7 seconds); charged beam every 20 seconds
The 3-second lock-on is already settled by your answer.
cover
What counts as cover from the slow beam?
A
Real stone: cover is whenever the straight line from the Ophan's eye to you passes through a wall, or a floor above you
It comes in low from one side, about 30 degrees up, so the wall on its side of a room shields you; the crypt and the keep's lower storey shield you everywhere.
B
Being inside any room counts as cover
Easier to read, but a room open to the sky would hide you from something looking straight into it.
The castle has no roofs today, so this decides how much shelter there is.
break
How much does the charged beam break?
A
It scorches the stone open: for the rest of the raid the slow beam passes through that room's walls, drawn burnt, on every machine
The smallest build, about two days: one synced list of scorched rooms and a burnt material, no new art. The walls stay solid to walk into.
B
It knocks the hit wall down
About two weeks: every room in every Age has its walls split from its floor in the art pipeline, plus a sync of fallen walls and updated guard paths.
C
It punches a hole where it hits
The largest and riskiest, several weeks: cutting meshes and rebuilding colliders while the game runs, kept the same on every machine.
Rooms are one piece today, so how much it breaks sets the size of the build.

wrapup.summary: A plan for the Ophan of Hours as a celestial threat far off in the sky, large enough to dwarf the castle, eye always on the players: a hum and screen shake, a slow beam that cover stops, and a one-hit charged beam that breaks cover.
wrapup.changing: Hunted raids end with the Ophan overhead. A beam takes an artifact and spares the carrier, or kills a player who carries none. Until the quota exists, only the test switch brings it.
wrapup.blocking: Your six picks under Choices. Nothing is built until you approve.
wrapup.next: On approval I log the decision, write the systems doc, file the steps as issues under #418 and build on the feature branch. It is not merged into staging until it passes.
